species: rat (Long-Evans; Royal College of Surgeons photoreceptor-degeneration model)
condition_other: Retinal photoreceptor degeneration (RCS rat model of retinitis pigmentosa)
readout_other: Multi-electrode array recordings from superior colliculus; fiber photometry (GCaMP8) from primary visual cortex; water-licking behavioral task; OCT, fundus imaging, and ERG; H&E and immunostaining (GFAP, CD68); RGC RNA-sequencing
direction_notes: Focused ultrasound activated remaining retinal ganglion cells in photoreceptor-degenerate (PD) retinas via acoustic radiation force, producing neuronal response patterns in the superior colliculus with amplitude similar to light-evoked responses, and drove learned behavioral responses comparable to light stimuli.
safety_notes: OCT/fundus imaging showed no structural retinal damage; ERG a- and b-wave amplitudes/latencies unchanged; histology showed no change in fundus structure, retinal layer thickness, microglial activation, or apoptosis after long-term (3 h, triweekly, 2 weeks) ultrasound exposure at pressures 50-100% above threshold.

exposures.label: Retina stimulation for electrophysiology and behavior (4.5 MHz default protocol)

device.model: custom single-channel and 16x16 2D ultrasound array transducers (4.4-4.5 MHz)

timing.protocol_description: Unless otherwise specified, the default US sequences used in this study were 10-ms pulse with 100% duty cycle. The frame interval was at least 6 seconds to ensure the stimulated neurons fully recovered after each stimulation. Initial validation used focused ultrasound stimuli (4.5 MHz, 10 ms, 2.83 MPa); the figure legend for the same experiment instead states 4.4 MHz, 10 ms, 3 MPa. Water-licking training and testing used 4.5 MHz, 20 ms, 2.9 MPa.

We subjected three healthy rats, each with one eye under ultrasound stimulation at frequencies of 3, 4.5, and 20 MHz. The pulses had a duration of 10 ms and a repetition frequency of 5 Hz, with pressure amplitudes surpassing the threshold by 50% (derated pressures were 5.8 MPa, 4.3 MPa, and 1.7 MPa). In the positive control group, the 20-MHz ultrasound were applied for three hours with a pressure 100% higher than the safe intensity (3.5 MPa vs 1.7 MPa, 10-ms pulse duration, and a repetition frequency of 5 Hz). Each rat underwent stimulation for 3 hours triweekly for two weeks (Day 1 to Day 13).

source_quotes.sham_type: To rule out any unintended cues like device noise or random mechanical stimulus, we conducted control tests, in which the ultrasound stimulated the skin between the eyeball and ear.
source_quotes.auditory_control: To prevent noise from equipment and devices from affecting the animals’ behavior, the animal table was surrounded by soundproofing acoustic foam (Acoustical Surfaces, Chaska, MN, USA).

flags.reason: Main text states 4.5 MHz/2.83 MPa for the initial validation experiment, but the Figure 1 legend states 4.4 MHz/3 MPa for the same experiment; both values are recorded.
Paper describes many partially-overlapping animal subsets for different sub-experiments (e.g., 3+3, 8, 8+8, 2+2, 3, 1) without ever stating a single overall total; not summed here.
Session counts differ by sub-experiment (single acute sessions vs 8-day behavioral training vs triweekly safety sessions over 2 weeks) with no single value applicable to all subjects.
The 3.5 MPa positive-control value applies specifically to the 20 MHz condition, not to all three frequencies; list combines values from different sub-conditions.
Electrophysiology and safety experiments used anesthetized rats, while water-licking behavioral sessions were performed in awake, head-fixed rats.
